[Medium/api] packages/lib/server/service/insightsBooking.ts:29 — InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions allows teamId to be omitted when scope is "team", weakening the discriminated-union contract so invalid calls compile and silently produce 1=0 after validation.

[Medium/test_gap] packages/lib/server/service/__tests__/insightsBooking.integration-test.ts:292 — Organization/team authorization tests only compare Prisma.Sql objects and never execute the new ANY(${array}) predicates against PostgreSQL, leaving migration-sensitive SQL paths unverified.

goldens.comment: In getBaseConditions(), the else if (filterConditions) and final else branches are unreachable. This is because getAuthorizationConditions() always returns a non-null Prisma.Sql object, making authConditions always truthy, which means only the first two if/else if conditions are ever evaluated.

Fetching userIdsFromOrg only when teamsFromOrg.length > 0 can exclude org-level members for orgs without child teams; consider deriving from teamIds (which includes orgId) or removing the guard so org-only orgs still include member user bookings.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [High/api] packages/lib/server/service/insightsBooking.ts:68 — Removing findMany() in favor of predicate-only getBaseConditions() breaks existing consumers and forces them to reimplement query execution; retain the method or migrate every caller.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly shows the removal of the `findMany()` method from InsightsBookingService (lines 66-78 in the old code are replaced with `getBaseConditions()`). The test file also shows the migration from using `service.findMany()` to using `service.getBaseConditions()` with raw SQL queries. This is a breaking API change - any existing consumers of `findMany()` would need to be updated. However, this is not a 'bug' per se, but rather an architectural/scope concern about breaking changes. The finding correctly identifies that this change forces callers to reimplement query execution.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/api] packages/lib/server/service/insightsBooking.ts:29 — InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions allows teamId to be omitted when scope is "team", weakening the discriminated-union contract so invalid calls compile and silently produce 1=0 after validation.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions at line 29 with 'teamId?: number' as optional regardless of scope. This type is used in the constructor (line 57) instead of the validated InsightsBookingServiceOptions. When scope is 'team' but teamId is omitted, the code at buildTeamAuthorizationCondition will receive options.teamId as undefined, which could cause issues. The validated schema (insightsBookingServiceOptionsSchema) requires teamId when scope is 'team', but the public type bypasses this validation, allowing invalid calls to compile. This is a real type-safety bug that weakens the discriminated union contract.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/test_gap] packages/lib/server/service/__tests__/insightsBooking.integration-test.ts:292 — Organization/team authorization tests only compare Prisma.Sql objects and never execute the new ANY(${array}) predicates against PostgreSQL, leaving migration-sensitive SQL paths unverified.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that most tests in the diff only compare Prisma.Sql objects using expect().toEqual() without actually executing the SQL against the database. Looking at the diff, tests at lines 292, 329, etc. compare the returned Prisma.sql template literals but don't run them. However, there IS one test ('should combine authorization and filter conditions') at line 477 that does execute the SQL via prisma.$queryRaw. The finding is partially valid - the ANY(${array}) syntax used in buildOrgAuthorizationCondition and buildTeamAuthorizationCondition is only tested via object comparison in most tests, not actual database execution. This is a legitimate test gap for migration-sensitive SQL, though the severity is reduced by the one integration test that does execute queries.
